Each reviewer judges only one aspect of a restaurant: food or service. A positive judgment means that aspect was good; a negative judgment means it was bad. Reviewers may use different label words, whose meanings can be inferred from their examples.
Alice and Bob judge the same aspect. Infer their criteria from the examples.

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The noodles tasted bad. The waiter was rude.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The dessert was delightful. The service was courteous.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The noodles tasted bad. The servers ignored us.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The burger was perfectly cooked. The waiter was rude.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The burger was perfectly cooked. The servers helped us promptly.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The noodles tasted bad. The waiter was polite.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The pizza was awful. The staff were careless.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The noodles tasted excellent. The waiter was polite.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The noodles tasted excellent. The service was courteous.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The noodles tasted bad. The service was discourteous.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The burger was badly burnt. The staff were careless.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The dessert tasted terrible. The servers ignored us.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The dessert was delightful. The servers ignored us.
Label: negative

Reviewer: Bob
Review: The burger was badly burnt. The waiter was polite.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The burger was perfectly cooked. The waiter was polite.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The pizza was delicious. The service was courteous.
Label: positive

Reviewer: Alice
Review: The entree was awful. The waitress treated us impolitely.
Give this reviewer's label for the review.<|im_end|>
